item.title: Quinten Post's $30M Offer Sheet Puts Warriors on the Clock
item.description:
A No. 52 draft pick just forced one of the NBA’s smartest front offices into a 36-hour decision worth $30 million.

That is the reality facing the Golden State Warriors this week. Quinten Post, the Dutch stretch big man they plucked late in the 2024 draft, has signed a three-year, $30 million offer sheet with the Memphis Grizzlies. Now the clock is ticking.

Quick Summary

  • Quinten Post signed a 3-year, $30 million offer sheet with the Memphis Grizzlies.
  • As a restricted free agent, the Warriors can match to keep him.
  • Golden State has until 11:59 p.m. ET on Tuesday, July 7 to decide.
  • Reporting suggests a match is unlikely after the team added veteran bigs.

Why Quinten Post’s Offer Sheet Matters

Restricted free agency is one of the NBA’s most fascinating pressure cookers, and the Quinten Post offer sheet is a textbook example of how it works.

item.title: Draymond Green Declines $27.7M, Becomes Free Agent
item.description:
Draymond Green Declines $27.7M, Becomes Free Agent

What if walking away from $27.7 million was actually the smartest money move of the offseason?

That’s exactly the gamble Draymond Green just made. On June 29, 2026, ESPN’s Shams Charania reported that the Golden State Warriors forward will decline his player option for the 2026-27 season and become a free agent — a decision that instantly reshaped the franchise’s pursuit of two of the biggest names in basketball.

item.title: LJ Cryer's Surprising Rise: How an Undrafted Guard Is Making Waves with the Warriors
item.description:
What happens when an undrafted guard from the Houston Cougars lands on one of the NBA’s most storied franchises — and actually starts making noise? That’s exactly the story of LJ Cryer, who has quietly carved out a meaningful role with the Golden State Warriors during the 2025–26 season.

Key Takeaways

  • LJ Cryer went undrafted in the 2025 NBA Draft but signed with the Golden State Warriors
  • He was waived during the preseason, then brought back and has since earned consistent minutes
  • Cryer returned to action on April 10 after missing two games due to illness
  • With Stephen Curry sidelined by a knee injury, Cryer’s role has grown significantly
  • He currently plays on a two-way contract, making him ineligible for the play-in tournament unless converted to a standard deal

LJ Cryer’s Path from Undrafted to the NBA

Not hearing your name called on draft night is a gut punch for any basketball player. For LJ Cryer, a standout guard at the Houston Cougars, the 2025 NBA Draft came and went without a selection. But that didn’t stop him.
